lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.title: Correction and reflection: family differences and dignity

objective: Learners explain why invented households with identical simulated income make different plans, and practise discussing money without ranking families.
scenario: Halle is an invented fifth grader in a pretend classroom exercise. Two made-up households each plan $900.00 of simulated monthly income: one puts a large share into a repair fund and a used car, the other into rent closer to work and no car at all. Both plans balance and neither household is real.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.
Discuss only the invented households on this sheet; do not describe any real family's income or spending.

tasks.directions: Read both invented plans with Halle. Each solves the problem of getting to work, and each pays for that solution in a different place. Describe the two approaches before evaluating either.

prompts.text: How does each of Halle's invented households solve the same problem, and where does each one spend to do it?

tasks.directions: A classmate says the car-free household is obviously smarter. Write a response that engages with the actual tradeoffs rather than agreeing or dismissing.

prompts.text: What would each household have to give up to switch to the other plan, and why does that make ranking them unreliable?

tasks.directions: Classroom talk about money can reach real families quickly.

prompts.text: What is one way to keep this discussion about the invented plans rather than about real classmates?

remediation: If a learner ranks the plans, remove the totals and re-read both as descriptions of constraints, then ask which constraint they would be willing to live under.
extension: Ask the learner to write a third $900.00 plan for Halle's exercise that solves the same problem a third way, and to name its tradeoff.
